title: Wipeout 2048
subtitle: Anti-gravity racing before the familiar future

body: Wipeout 2048 is Studio Liverpool's PlayStation Vita racing game, first released in Japan on 19 January 2012. Set before the original Wipeout, its championship runs through the years 2048 to 2050, bringing anti-gravity craft into streets that still resemble a recognisable city. The tracks therefore sit between ordinary urban roads and the more distant future associated with the series. Racing keeps the familiar combination of high speed, airbrakes and weapons, with the Vita's screen presenting the movement in the player's hands rather than across a television.

The craft float above the course, so steering involves anticipating their movement instead of simply pointing at a corner. Airbrakes help tighten a line, while speed pads reward positioning before the next turn. Weapon pickups can change the balance between protecting a lead and interrupting an opponent. The player gradually learns where the track offers room for a correction and where a poor approach becomes a collision. Different event conditions make those same routes serve more than a conventional race against a full field of competitors.

Wipeout 2048 was developed alongside the Vita's arrival and became one of the handheld's launch titles. Its online features included interaction with Wipeout HD on PlayStation 3, linking the portable release to an existing community. Reviewers praised the presentation while noting long loading times and other technical compromises. The game was Studio Liverpool's final production before the studio closed in 2012. Its tracks later joined Wipeout HD and the Fury expansion in the PlayStation 4 Omega Collection, giving this earlier chapter of the fictional championship another home.
